The Fairhope Single Tax Corporation

Fairhope started in 1894 as a single-tax colony. The Fairhope Single Tax Corporation still owns land and leases it to residents, with about 1,800 leaseholds covering more than 4,000 acres in and around the city.

If your house stands on leased land, the lease itself may set the rules for a transfer, and a standard deed will not tell the whole story. Ask the corporation and your closing agent which steps apply before you accept an offer. If you own the lot outright as a fee-simple parcel, none of this touches you and the sale follows the ordinary Alabama route.

Selling an inherited or older owner's house

Fairhope skews older than most Alabama cities. About 56.9 percent of households were married couples, 27.8 percent were one person living alone, and 17.7 percent were a person 65 or older living alone. Behind those numbers are owners moving closer to family, households coping with a death, and estates waiting to be settled.

For heirs, the probate and title questions often take longer than any repair. Find out from your closing agent which court papers must exist before a deed can be signed, and ask that on day one.

What to expect after you accept an offer

Once you sign a contract, the title search begins. The examiner reads the record for liens, unpaid taxes and ownership gaps, and reports anything that has to be cleared before the deed can pass. In Fairhope this is also the moment to confirm whether the lot is a leasehold, since that changes who must approve the transfer.

Next, you and the buyer settle the repair question. With a financed buyer, an inspection can bring a request for fixes or a lower price. With a cash buyer who accepts the house as it is, that step mostly drops away.

The last stage is signing. You sign the deed and the settlement statement, the closing agent pays off any lender, and the deed goes to the Baldwin County probate office. Bring a photo ID and every key, remote and garage opener you have.

Selling with a mortgage, a lien or taxes owed

An open mortgage can be paid at closing out of the sale proceeds. The lender gives a payoff figure, the closing agent sends it, and the lien is released. The same goes for a past-due tax bill, which is cleared from the proceeds so the buyer receives a clean title.

If you are not sure what is owed, ask for the payoff and the tax balance before you list or accept an offer. That tells you what you would actually keep, and it avoids surprises at the table.

Coastal conditions buyers ask about

Fairhope has a humid subtropical climate, and a bayfront setting makes buyers and insurers curious about wind, rain and water. The ground runs from sea level at the bay up to about 122 feet in the center, so the distance from the shoreline colors how a buyer reads flood risk.

  • Roof and windows: with coastal wind, record their age and condition.
  • Insurance: keep the current policy, premium and any claim history handy.
  • Moisture: look for rot, mold and damaged siding after storms.

A cash buyer prices those items in and does not wait on a lender's insurance demands.

Permits and school zones

City building and zoning rules overlap with Baldwin County's. If a garage, deck or extra room went up without a permit, the buyer's inspector or the title examiner will probably ask. Check with city and county offices about what is needed before you list.

Public schools run through Baldwin County Public Schools. About 39 percent of the city's high-school-age students attend Daphne High School to the north, since Fairhope High sits in the southernmost part of town. Tell buyers which zone your address falls into, after confirming it with the county school office.

How a Fairhope sale closes

The sale is final once the deed reaches the Baldwin County probate office. At that point Alabama's recordation tax applies: 50 cents per $500 of value under section 40-22-1, with the real purchase price shown alongside the deed.

Property tax comes due October 1 and turns delinquent after December 31. The lot type decides who you need to talk to first.

Paperwork to gather first

  • Order a payoff statement for any mortgage or home equity line.
  • Collect the deed, the survey and permits for any additions.
  • Ask the closing agent how the year's tax will be divided.

Keeping all of it in one folder shortens the title search and lets you answer a buyer's first questions the same day. A lien or an unclear owner is far easier to handle weeks before closing than on signing day.

Three ways to sell in Fairhope

You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer. A listing reaches the most buyers, but it means preparing the house, hosting showings and waiting on a buyer's loan approval and appraisal. Selling on your own saves the commission, and you handle the marketing, screening and paperwork yourself.

A cash sale trades some price for speed and certainty. If the house is on leased land, needs repairs or belongs to an estate, the simpler path is often worth more to you than a longer listing.

What a cash offer removes

Sellers here include older owners, heirs, landlords tired of storm repairs and people leaving the area. A direct cash offer takes out the showings and the repair list, and you choose the closing date.

  • Estate sales where heirs live far away.

It is the organization that has leased land to Fairhope residents since the city's founding in 1894. It has about 1,800 leaseholds covering more than 4,000 acres in and around the city.

Possibly, but the lease terms control the transfer. Ask the Single Tax Corporation and your closing agent what the lease requires before signing a contract.

Pelham in brief

Pelham is a Shelby County city in the Birmingham metro area, about 20 miles south of downtown Birmingham and 72 miles north of Montgomery. It incorporated on July 10, 1964, covers about 39 square miles at roughly 830 feet of elevation, and uses ZIP code 35124.

Oak Mountain State Park, the largest state park in Alabama, lies within the city, so many house hunters arrive for the trails and lakes as much as for the homes. That is worth a line in any listing.

Because so much of Pelham was built after 1980, much of its housing is a few decades old. Inspectors on houses of that age commonly look at roof coverings and flashing, heating and air systems, water heaters and original windows. Shelby County as a whole is 78.1 percent owner-occupied, so most of your competition on a listing is other owners, not rentals.

Commuting and travel

US Route 31 runs straight through Pelham, and Interstate 65 reaches the city at exits 242 and 246. ClasTran provides weekday dial-a-ride service, and Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport is in the next county over. US 231 and US 280 also cross Shelby County.

Many residents commute north into Birmingham, and others work locally. Give buyers the real distance to the interstate and to Birmingham when you describe the house, because commute length drives much of the conversation in a suburb like this.

Schools

Pelham City Schools has run the city's public schools since July 1, 2014, when it split from the Shelby County system. It has two elementary schools, one middle school and Pelham High School. Before the split, some parts of Pelham beside Chelsea attended Chelsea schools. Houses in that part of town can still prompt boundary questions, so check assignments by address before quoting them.

Private options in the county include Briarwood Christian School and Westminster School at Oak Mountain. Jefferson State's Shelby-Hoover campus and the University of Montevallo are within reach.

Shelby County

Shelby County has about 223,000 residents, ranks sixth in Alabama by population and has its seat in Columbiana. Its 2020 population was 223,024 and a 2025 estimate is 238,552. Growth came from the interstate and US 31 and spread across Pelham, Helena, Alabaster and Chelsea. A Pelham seller therefore competes with houses in several nearby cities, each with its own school district.

Farmland, rail and later the interstate built the county. It was founded on February 7, 1818, and went from 38,037 people in 1970 to 66,298 in 1980. The first county seat, Shelbyville, stood in what is now Pelham beginning in 1820, before the seat moved to Columbiana in 1826.

Slopes, creeks and drainage

The southern end of the Appalachians crosses Shelby County, with Oak Mountain and Double Oak Mountain, while other parts are flat. Water drains mainly to the Cahaba and Coosa rivers.

A house on a slope may bring drainage, retaining wall and foundation questions. A house near a creek bed deserves a closer look at the flood zone. Learn the answers before a buyer asks, since an unexplained crack or a damp crawl space is the kind of thing that cuts an offer.

The city has its own building inspector, permits clerk, revenue department, waterworks and city clerk, and several of them touch a house sale. The building inspector and permits clerk handle work done without paperwork, waterworks handles utility accounts and the revenue department handles local licenses.

If a prior owner finished a basement or added a room, ask the city whether a permit was pulled before you list. A missing permit can slow a financed sale, though it is less of a barrier for a buyer who purchases as is.

Deed tax and property tax

Alabama Code section 40-22-1 puts a recordation tax of 50 cents on each $500 of value in a deed. The probate judge collects it before recording, and a recording fee is separate.

Property taxes come due October 1 and become delinquent after December 31. The Shelby County offices in Columbiana hold the parcel records and can supply a payoff figure. Ask for it early so the closing statement is accurate.

If you owe a mortgage or back taxes

A balance on the house does not stop a sale. The title company gets a payoff letter from your lender and a tax figure from the county, then pays both at closing out of your proceeds. You receive what is left.

Back taxes, liens and unpaid utility bills show up in the title search, and each is settled at the same table. Request the search early so you can see the full list and decide whether the offer still makes sense once everything is paid. Ask the closer to walk you through each line on the settlement statement before you sign.

If you are behind on the mortgage, tell the buyer. A firm closing date can matter more than a higher number when a lender is waiting, and a cash buyer can often move on a schedule that a financed sale cannot match.

Ask for the offer in writing, confirm who pays closing costs and read the contract before you sign. Compare the offer to the likely net from a listing after repairs, fees and the carrying cost of the months a house may sit. We buy Pelham houses as they are and you are free to decline.

Before you sign

Bring a photo ID, the deed, the latest tax bill and your lender's payoff information to the closing. If the house is part of an estate, bring the paperwork showing who may sign. Ask whether the buyer's offer depends on a loan or an inspection, and ask what happens to your deposit if the sale falls through.

Make a note of what is staying and what is going. Appliances, window coverings and fixtures should be listed in the contract so nobody argues about them at the walkthrough. Turn off or transfer utilities only after the closing date is firm.
